ingredients: 2 (15-oz) cans black beans, drained and rinsed
2–3 chipotle peppers in adobo, minced, plus 1 tbsp of the sauce (7-oz can)
2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp smoked paprika, salt
recipes.intro: Meal-prep burrito bowls with a chipotle kick. The first cook in the meal-prep series.
notes: Tip: slightly undercook the rice if you plan to microwave the bowls — it'll finish in the reheat without going soft.
steps: Cook the brown rice per package; fluff and squeeze half a lime over it.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Sauté onion 3–4 min until softened, add garlic, cumin, paprika, and chipotles; stir 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add ground turkey, break it up, and cook until browned and cooked through, about 8 min.
Stir in black beans and corn; cook 4–5 min until heated through. Season with salt and remaining lime juice.
In a separate hot pan, quickly char the bell peppers 2–3 min so they stay crisp — no mush.
Portion into containers: rice, turkey-bean mix, peppers. Pack the Greek yogurt separately and dollop on when eating.
recipes.title: Chipotle Turkey & Black Bean Burrito Bowls

ingredients: Paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, Goya Adobo seasoning
recipes.intro: One-pan chicken and rice, extracted from the creator's post. Tagged #mealprep by the creator.
steps: Dice the bell pepper, onion, and carrots; mince the garlic.
Season both sides of the chicken thighs with paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, and Adobo.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sear chicken ~4 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add the vegetables and garlic with the butter. Sauté a few minutes until fragrant.
Add the rice and toast with the vegetables 1–2 minutes.
Pour in the broth and stir in the bouillon. Taste and adjust salt/bouillon.
Nestle the chicken back on top of the rice, pouring in any collected juices.
Cover and cook on medium-low ~20 minutes, until rice is tender and chicken hits 165°F.
Rest covered off the heat 5–10 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.
recipes.title: One-Pan Chicken & Rice (Arroz con Pollo)

ingredients: 4" piece ginger, sliced into coins (no need to peel)
Garnish: Thai basil, sliced green onions, sesame seeds, drizzle of chili oil (optional)
recipes.intro: Braised short rib in a coconut curry broth over rice. Extracted from Brita Cooks' recipe page.
notes: Alternate methods: Dutch oven — braise covered at 325°F for ~3 hours. Slow cooker — low 8 hours or high 4–5 hours (sear and bloom the curry paste in a skillet first).
Full-fat canned coconut milk makes the creamiest broth; jasmine rice recommended.
Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge (store ribs, broth, and rice separately) or 3 months in the freezer.
steps: Trim excess fat from the short ribs and season generously with kosher salt on all sides. Set the pressure cooker to sauté, add the oil, and sear the ribs deeply on all sides until well browned. Transfer to a plate.
Drain most of the rendered fat, leaving about a tablespoon. Add the red curry paste and cook 2–3 minutes, stirring frequently and scraping up the browned bits, until slightly darkened and fragrant.
Stir in the shallots, garlic, and ginger. Return the short ribs to the pot, add soy sauce, fish sauce, and brown sugar, then pour in enough beef stock to mostly submerge the ribs (3–4 cups).
Seal the lid and pressure cook on high for 45 minutes.
Natural release for 15 minutes, then quick release any remaining pressure.
Transfer the ribs to a plate; once cool enough to handle, shred the meat off the bones.
Strain the broth, discarding the shallots, garlic, and ginger. Return the broth to the pot, stir in the coconut milk, and adjust with a little more soy sauce or fish sauce to taste.
Divide rice between bowls, top with shredded short rib, ladle the broth over, and finish with green onions, Thai basil, and sesame seeds.
recipes.title: Spicy Short Rib Coconut Curry Brothy Rice Bowls

recipes.attribution: Mom's recipe, translated from her Spanish original
ingredients: 1 can black beans (15.5 oz) — save the liquid from the can
recipes.intro: Mom's arroz congrí, translated from her Spanish original into plain text for an Apple Note.
notes: Note from Dad: "I just cooked it on the rice cooker and it tastes delicious."
steps: Open the can of beans, drain the liquid, and save it for later.
In the pot where you'll make the rice, heat the oil over medium-high heat. When hot, add the sofrito and the chicken bouillon cubes, stir, and cook for one minute.
Add the rice and stir so it mixes well with the sofrito. Then add the black beans, the bay leaf, and the olives (optional).
Add the 2 cups of water and the bean liquid, stir, and taste the water to check the seasoning. If it's bland, add a little salt.
Cook until you see the rice is drier, then stir, cover, and turn to low heat until the rice is done (about 20 to 30 minutes).
recipes.title: Arroz Congrí — Mom's Recipe

ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
2 bunches lacinato kale, stems removed, leaves chopped
1 jar (8 oz) sun-dried tomatoes, drained and sliced
1 sprig fresh rosemary (leaves stripped and minced), plus extra for garnish
1 tsp salt, ½ tsp black pepper, ¼ tsp red pepper flakes
recipes.intro: Braised chicken thighs with beans and kale. Cooked as the Oct 10 batch.
notes: Tip: if you're feeding two on Tuesday, this scales cleanly — just double everything and use a full bunch of kale per person.

Rice-serving tip: cook the rice separately — don't add it to the braise, or it'll go mushy sitting in the liquid all week. Just portion rice + braise into the same containers. Go with ½ cup cooked per serving (~110 calories). The beans already bring plenty of carbs and fiber, so a modest scoop keeps the lunch from becoming a food coma. That puts each portion around ~570 calories, ~42g protein, ~11g fiber.
recipes.nutrition: ~460 cal, ~40g protein, ~9g fiber, ~18g fat, ~28g carbs per serving
steps: Pat the chicken thighs dry and season both sides with salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes.
Heat the olive oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the thighs 4–5 minutes per side until browned. Transfer to a plate (they don't need to be cooked through).
Reduce heat to medium. Add garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, and rosemary; sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken broth and scrape up the browned bits. Add the beans and nestle the chicken back in.
Simmer uncovered 15–20 minutes, until the chicken registers 165°F and the broth thickens slightly.
Stir in the kale in batches, cover, and cook 4–5 minutes until just wilted — it should keep some body.
Shred or slice the chicken into bite-sized pieces, stir back through, and finish with lemon juice. Taste and adjust salt.
Divide into 5 containers. Keeps 4 days refrigerated; freezes up to 2 months.
recipes.title: Garlic-Herb Chicken Thighs with Cannellini Beans & Kale

recipes.attribution: Adapted from Hot Thai Kitchen's pad kra pao — http://hot-thai-kitchen.com/holy-basil-stir-fry/
recipes.delivered: Oct 12, 2026 (adapted from Hot Thai Kitchen's pad kra pao, scaled ×3)
ingredients: 12–18 Thai bird's eye chilies (12 = medium heat across the batch)
3 bell peppers, chopped into bite-size pieces
4 1/2 cups Thai basil leaves, loosely packed
Neutral oil: a thin film for searing (skip if your skillet is nonstick) + 1 tbsp for the chili-garlic paste
Sauce (mix in a bowl first): 3 tbsp oyster-style sauce
Sauce: 1 1/2 tbsp tamari (in place of dark/black soy sauce)
To serve: 3 cups uncooked brown jasmine rice (rice cooker, brown rice setting, extra time)
recipes.intro: The real-deal version: chilies and garlic pounded into a paste, chicken seared hard before the sauce goes in. Salty, spicy, fragrant. Cooked Oct 12, 2026.
notes: Reheating: sprinkle a teaspoon or two of water over the top before microwaving to loosen the sauce.
You ordered 3 lb of chicken — this recipe uses 2 lb (Pailin's ratio). Use all 3 if you want it meatier (~45g protein/serving), or freeze the third pound.
No wok needed; a large skillet on full heat works. Don't crowd it — if your skillet is small, sear the chicken in two batches.
The fried egg is traditional but doesn't reheat well — skip it on prep portions, fry fresh if you want one on serving day.
Jarred garlic works in the paste, but fresh is better here since it's a main flavor — your call.

Cook corrections (Oct 12 cook): searing in stainless steel — use a thin film of oil, heated until shimmering (supersedes the earlier no-oil dry-sear guidance). Tamari stands in for dark/black soy sauce (Sprouts doesn't carry it). Jarred garlic was used. Actual cook used regular basil — Sprouts substituted it for the Thai basil in the pickup order.
steps: Start the rice first — brown jasmine takes a while. Use your cooker's brown rice setting.
Pound the chilies into a fine paste with a mortar and pestle. Add the garlic and pound into a rough paste. (No mortar? Mince both as finely as you can — the paste is what makes it fragrant.)
Stir the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves. Pick the basil leaves and set them by the stove.

Heat your largest skillet over HIGH heat with a thin film of oil (skip the oil if your skillet is nonstick). Add the chicken and spread it out. Sear without moving until the underside is browned. Toss and keep cooking until the liquid evaporates and it starts to sizzle and brown again — this browning is where the flavor comes from. Season with a pinch of salt.
Push the chicken to one side. Add 1 tbsp oil and the chili-garlic paste. Sauté until the garlic starts to turn golden, about 30 seconds.
Toss everything together. Pour in the sauce and toss until the chicken is cooked through and coated, 1–2 minutes.
Add the bell peppers and onion. Toss 1–2 minutes until crisp-tender.
Turn OFF the heat. Add all the basil and toss just until wilted, about 20 seconds. Taste — more fish sauce for salt, a pinch of sugar for balance.
Portion over rice into containers. Refrigerate up to 4 days.
recipes.title: Thai Basil Chicken (Pad Kra Pao) — Meal Prep

ingredients: Marinade: 1½ lb boneless, skinless chicken breast
Marinade: ½ cup fat-free plain Greek yogurt
Marinade: 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated or minced
Marinade: 1 tsp paprika or Kashmiri chili powder
Sauce: 1 medium yellow onion, finely diced
Sauce: 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated or minced
Sauce: 1 tsp paprika or Kashmiri chili powder
Sauce: ¼–½ tsp cayenne pepper, optional
Sauce: ½ cup chicken broth or water
Sauce: 1 tsp salt, plus more to taste
Sauce: ¼ cup chopped fresh cilantro or parsley
To serve: Brown or white rice
recipes.intro: Yogurt-marinated chicken in a creamy spiced tomato sauce. Meal-prep friendly.
notes: Meal prep: divide into 4 containers with about ¼ of the tikka masala and 1¼–1½ cups cooked rice each. Keep a generous amount of sauce per portion — the rice absorbs some during storage. Let cool briefly, then refrigerate promptly.
Reheating: microwave loosely covered in 60–90 second intervals, stirring the tikka masala between intervals if needed.
steps: Cut the chicken into roughly 1½-inch pieces. Combine the Greek yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, ginger, garam masala, cumin, paprika or Kashmiri chili powder, salt, and black pepper in a bowl. Add the chicken and mix until thoroughly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (4–24 hours for best flavor).

Heat a large skillet over medium-high to high heat with a little oil. Remove the chicken from the marinade, letting excess drip off. Sear in batches without overcrowding, 2–3 minutes per side, until browned (it doesn't need to be fully cooked). Transfer to a plate.

Reduce heat to medium. Add the butter and olive oil, then the diced onion; cook 5–7 minutes until softened and lightly browned. Add the garlic and ginger and cook about 1 minute. Add the garam masala, cumin, coriander, paprika or Kashmiri chili powder, turmeric, and cayenne (if using); cook 30–45 seconds, stirring constantly.

Add the crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits, add 1 tsp salt, and simmer gently uncovered for 10–15 minutes until slightly reduced and richer. If the tomatoes taste too acidic, add 1 tsp sugar.

Return the chicken and any accumulated juices to the skillet. Simmer gently 5–8 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and reaches 165°F. Reduce heat to low, stir in the heavy cream, and simmer gently 2–3 more minutes — don't aggressively boil after adding the cream. Taste and adjust salt, cayenne, garam masala, or a small squeeze of lemon juice.
Turn off the heat and stir in the chopped cilantro or parsley. Serve over brown or white rice.
recipes.title: Chicken Tikka Masala
